solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Piece of information I came across after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for came across is read backwards

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them; past tense met

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a fact they stumbled on after a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests politics, but 'after revolution' is the reversal signal applied to the meeting word, which then follows I.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single unit of news or data, such as an entry in a report.

clue.text: Bar used by swingers

parts.note: a circus acrobat's horizontal bar hung from ropes on which performers swing; the surface hints at a pub for wife-swappers

explanation.surface: A nightspot frequented by partner-swapping couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a drinking venue and 'swingers' a lifestyle, but it is the acrobat's swinging bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapeze is the suspended crossbar that circus performers swing from.

clue.text: From limo, telephone place where drivers stay?

indicators.note: the letters come from within the run of words limo, telephone, spanning the two

explanation.surface: Phoning from a limousine to book somewhere for chauffeurs to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside hotel built for motorists, who park beside their rooms.

clue.text: Written work about border plant

indicators.note: the written-work word goes about, or around, the border word

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language, as opposed to verse
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a flower growing in a garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' tempts as a garden bed, but here it is just an edge; 'about' wraps the writing word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring-flowering woodland plant.

clue.text: Fix leg

definitions.meaning: to fasten something in place with a pointed fastener

explanation.surface: An instruction to mend a broken limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinning attaches things; pins is colloquial slang for legs.

clue.text: Batting team dismissed comprehensively

parts.note: in cricket the batting side is said to be in
a side is a team
a dismissed batsman is out

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the batting team was all out, thoroughly beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket terms: the side batting is 'in', a dismissed batsman is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something inside out is to know it thoroughly, in every detail.

clue.text: Income level in Parisian's street

indicators.note: the word for level sits in the French word for street

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: Someone's earnings are measured by the street they live on in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian's' signals a French word; 'in' places the level word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in, especially an organisation's or state's income.

clue.text: Heather after second alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the heather word comes after the letter for second

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Heather orders a cocktail after her second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant LING.
explanation.definitionFit: A sling is a cocktail of spirit, sugar and water or juice, as in the gin sling.

clue.text: Resort town possesses elements husband overlooked

parts.note: has means owns or possesses

indicators.note: the husband letter is overlooked, missed out of the word for elements

parts.note: things are items or components

explanation.surface: A seaside town lists its components, though a husband was left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked' drops H from THINGS to leave TINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings is a seaside resort on the Sussex coast in southern England, famous for the 1066 battle.

clue.text: Conceal very ugly lie

indicators.note: an ugly version of the word is a mangled, misshapen one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to cover up a nasty falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: To veil something is to cover or hide it, as with a cloth over the face.

clue.text: Fine spring

definitions.meaning: a source of water from the ground

explanation.surface: A pleasant season.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means healthy or satisfactory, and also a water source sunk or rising in the ground.

clue.text: Mark engaging in a bit of playful repartee

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it on or hold it, so the mark word holds the words in a

parts.note: a badge is a mark or emblem

explanation.surface: A man named Mark joins in a little witty back-and-forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name; it is BADGE, which 'engaging' wraps around IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, teasing banter exchanged in conversation.

clue.text: Definitely not taking funny money in bars

indicators.note: the rearranged money letters go in the word for bars

parts.note: to bar is to ban, so bars are bans

indicators.note: funny money is odd or strange, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Refusing counterfeit cash in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs, but it is the verb sense of prohibitions; 'funny' scrambles the cash word and 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic phrase for certainly not, not in the least.

clue.text: Reputation our sailors have across the East

indicators.note: the Royal Navy letters stretch across, either side of, the East letter

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is Britain's own navy
E is the abbreviation for East
to own is to have or possess

explanation.surface: The Royal Navy's good name extends across eastern waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our sailors' is the British setter's own navy; 'across' wraps it around the East letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame or widespread acclaim, a name that is well known.

clue.text: Plump single mother, ideal

parts.note: to plump for something is to opt for it
I is the Roman numeral one
mum is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A single mum who is overweight is described as perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, as in plump for.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the best or most favourable, as an adjective.

clue.text: Unique type of switch saving energy?

indicators.note: saving here means keeping or holding inside, so the switch word holds the energy letter

parts.note: an on-off switch toggles between two states
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rare kind of light switch that cuts electricity use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like economy; it puts E inside ON-OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one of a kind, done or made only once, is singular and without equal.

clue.text: Male supervisor in favour of elevated title

parts.note: for means supporting or in favour of

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevated means raised up, so the title word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a name is a title

explanation.surface: A man in charge supports a grander job title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reads as a promotion, but in a down clue it means the title word is written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreman is a worker who supervises a crew, traditionally a man.

clue.text: Swindle to attract scorn

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
to tempt is to entice or attract

explanation.surface: A fraud designed to draw ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is disdain, the feeling that something is worthless.

clue.text: A diamond ring turned up in the end?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means flipped upwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a diamond is a gem
o is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A diamond engagement ring finally appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'appeared' but reverses A GEM O.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so figuratively the end; the question mark flags the indirect sense.

clue.text: Gold used by artist creates atmosphere

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A painter's gilding produces a certain mood.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or air surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: A medic going round hospital when necessary

indicators.note: the medic word goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: a doc is a doctor
h is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A doctor does rounds of the hospital as needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc means arranged for a particular need as it arises, not planned.

clue.text: Party in power lacking leader

indicators.note: the power word is missing its first letter, its leader

parts.note: steam powers engines

explanation.surface: A political party in government without anyone to head it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics, but it is a group on one side; STEAM loses S.
explanation.definitionFit: A party can be a group working together, as a search party is a team.

clue.text: Object of loathing and hate a man smashed

indicators.note: smashed means broken to pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone loathes and hates a man who wrecked something.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something or someone intensely detested.

clue.text: Function of a court

explanation.surface: A court's duty or role.
explanation.definitionFit: To function is to operate or perform, as in a machine that does its job.

clue.text: Head of menagerie, maestro trained monkey

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
trained suggests reshaped or put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The zookeeper in charge, a skilled conductor, has taught an ape tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of menagerie' suggests a zookeeper, but gives only an initial; 'trained' scrambles the conductor word.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American tree-dwelling primate.

clue.text: Walking stick, article found in church

indicators.note: the article word is found in, placed inside, the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone's walking aid has turned up in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' reads as discovered, but it puts the article inside the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane is a stick used as a support when walking.
